parsed.explanation: Trans visibility is legally framed as pornographic/propaganda material punishable by imprisonment, with documented police detentions of eight trans people in one month, beatings, coerced charges and custody abuse. Police collect passport details and photos, prisons leave LGBT prisoners unprotected with staff encouraging abuse, and there is no anti-discrimination, hate-crime or regional-court recourse. State media crime-free framing as paedophilia/foreign weapon and 84% public hostility amplify outing consequences. No documented execution for trans identity keeps it above 0.05, but state-directed targeting with no remedy places it in Severe Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: Police collect passport details and photographs at cruising areas; 2004 threat that foreigners attending LGBT workshops would be expelled; foreign document acceptance not established.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy or visibility can trigger investigation under depiction/propaganda laws, leading to detention or expulsion.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: 15+ LGBTQ people detained in Sep 2024, eight trans, mostly hooliganism and two pornography; reported beatings, coerced charges and physical/psychological custody abuse; prison staff encourage abuse of LGBT prisoners.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest for presentation/depiction flows into unprotected custody where abuse is tolerated, with little expectation of redress.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: LGBT venues closed, raided or intermittently tolerated; capital club closed and pride party raided historically. Specific bathroom/facility rules not documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National criminal framing applies across capital and provincial cities in the subnational evidence; no documented local protective divergence.

care_services.exposure: Qualified psychological help generally unavailable; no transgender-specific facilities documented; emergency or routine care access for visitors not documented.
care_services.interaction: Detention abuse and lack of care compound risk; scarcity is documented generally, visitor-specific care denial is uncertain.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: 2024 definition treats depictions of trans people as pornography (up to 4 years, 13 involving children); 2026 law bans propaganda including gender reassignment; state media equate LGBTI identity with paedophilia and foreign threat.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Law and propaganda make public presence itself prosecutable and license police/societal hostility; enforcement described as immediate.

minors_guardians.exposure: Penalties rise to 13 years where children are involved; propaganda law expressly concerns child-related dissemination, increasing family travel exposure if transition-related depiction/content is present.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian's transition-related material or a minor's presence can aggravate charges; no protective family immigration recognition.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 84% in 2017 poll said homosexuality should not be accepted; open LGBT people face harassment and violence; police reported beating LGBTQ people during arrest and do not investigate homophobic motives.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Societal hostility plus police perpetration and non-investigation removes street-level protection after outing.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination or hate-crime prohibition, no SOGI persecution protection, no regional human-rights court, no hate-crime data since 2015, no national reporting contact.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Absence of recourse applies across police, custody and violence axes; civil-society figures are the only incident source.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: criminalised presentation/depiction, routine police arrest, beatings and illusory remedies. Lower severity than 0.15-A only insofar as no capital provision for this offence is documented and documented detentions are a monthly wave rather than months-long pretrial norm.

Worse than 0.25-A: 0.25-A has short custody, occasional court reversals and no execution; here custody abuse, beatings, coerced charges, police data collection and grouped-with-paedophilia criminal framing show state-directed targeting with no functioning remedy.

Materially below 0.35-B: 0.35-B involves hours-long stops, fines and rarely imprisonment with courts formally accepting complaints. Here imprisonment up to four years, documented abuse and police as perpetrators make consequences after outing substantially more severe.

Above 0.05-A: no documented execution or lethal custody pathway for trans visitors in this dossier. Death penalty is retained generally but not shown applied to trans depiction/propaganda cases, so lethal outcome is not established as foreseeable.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime interaction is adverse at every stage: state law turns visibility into pornography/propaganda, police actively collect data, detain and beat, custody abuse is tolerated, and no legal or regional remedy exists. Public hostility and official threat-framing reinforce police action rather than restraining it. Document acceptance, facility rules and visitor care remain uncertain, which cannot offset documented targeting. For a minor, the child-involvement penalty escalation adds exposure. This is state-perpetrated, not merely societal, risk.
